title: Extract strings for translation (i18n)
when: The user wants the app or site available in more than one language, or to move hard coded text into translation files.
inputs: the files with user facing text
prompt:
Goal: All user facing strings live in one JSON file per language, looked up by stable keys, with a working language switch.
Steps:
1. Find every user facing string: HTML text, attributes (alt, title, placeholder, aria-label), and strings in scripts, including errors.
2. Create locales/en.json and locales/pt.json with flat, meaningful keys (cart.empty, cart.checkout), never sentences as keys.
3. Mark HTML with data-i18n="cart.empty" (and data-i18n-attr="aria-label:cart.close" for attributes) and apply with textContent.
4. Write t(key, params) that looks up the active locale, falls back to English, and replaces {name} placeholders.
5. Pick the language from a saved choice, then navigator.language, then the default; set <html lang> on change.
6. Keep whole sentences per key so translators can reorder words.
Quality bar:
- No user facing text is left in code.
- Both locale files have the same keys.
- Missing keys show the fallback, never the raw key.
Pitfalls:
- Concatenating fragments ("You have " + n + " items").
- Translating with innerHTML, which opens injection holes.
- Forgetting attribute text and error messages.
Verify:
- [ ] Locale files are valid JSON with matching keys.
- [ ] Switching language updates text and lang.
- [ ] Scripts parse.
- [ ] Placeholders are replaced.
Output: locales/<lang>.json files, i18n.js with t() and the switch, and HTML marked with data-i18n.

examples.input: quero meu site em português e inglês
examples.output: locales/pt.json and en.json with 48 keys, data-i18n attributes, switcher saved per visitor
